beats.visual: Soft graphite storybook close-up of one observer's eye in sharp pencil focus while, deeper in the frame, another everyday person stretches into a yawn; the yawning mouth is softly reflected in the observer's pupil, with muted sage and straw colored-pencil accents on warm cream paper.
beats.purpose: show the visual system noticing another person's yawning jaw
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme eye close-up + distant yawning figure + quiet household doorway + reflected mouth in pupil + diagonal depth composition
beats.continuity: moves away from the opening workshop into a neutral everyday subject-world example, beginning with the first visual cue

beats.narration_slice: The brain recognizes a familiar human action.
beats.visual: Centered graphite side-profile head silhouette on cream paper, with a tiny hand-drawn yawning figure nested inside the softly shaded brain area like a remembered action; sparse broken hatching and muted powder-blue pencil tint keep the concept intuitive rather than medical.
beats.purpose: show the brain identifying the observed movement as a familiar human action
beats.visual_fingerprint: single profile head silhouette + miniature yawning figure inside brain + abstract cream-paper field + centered anatomical-metaphor composition
beats.continuity: shifts from the external sight cue to an internal recognition diagram

beats.visual: Over-the-shoulder medium shot in a simple waiting-room setting: a seated person abruptly turns their head toward someone yawning across the room, with two faint graphite motion arcs behind the turning face and peripheral chairs dissolving into unfinished pencil strokes.
beats.purpose: show attention rapidly orienting toward the yawn
beats.visual_fingerprint: over-shoulder observer + sudden head turn + waiting-room chairs + off-axis yawner + motion arcs sweeping across frame
beats.continuity: returns from the internal diagram to an observable reaction in a different everyday setting

beats.narration_slice: Perception and movement systems may prime a matching response.
beats.visual: Minimal pencil diagram showing an eye silhouette on the upper left and a jaw-and-neck silhouette on the lower right, connected by a soft chain of ghosted graphite echoes that gradually change from seeing a yawn to preparing the same mouth-opening motion; no labels or interface elements.
beats.purpose: show a possible link between perceiving the action and preparing a matching movement
beats.visual_fingerprint: eye symbol + jaw-neck silhouette + descending chain of ghosted motion echoes + blank paper field + diagonal cause-to-response layout
beats.continuity: abstracts the previous head turn into a simple perception-to-movement sequence

beats.narration_slice: That can make your own yawn easier to trigger.
beats.visual: Three-quarter close shot of the Red Horned Everyman in a neutral reading nook, calmly trying to suppress a yawn as one hand hovers near his mouth; his jaw has just begun to open, eyes slightly watering, with a faint ghosted wider-open jaw behind him suggesting the response becoming easier.
beats.purpose: show the host beginning to yawn after the response has been primed
beats.visual_fingerprint: Red Horned Everyman three-quarter close-up + restrained hand-to-mouth reaction + reading nook + ghosted wider jaw echo + asymmetrical portrait composition
beats.continuity: turns the mechanism diagram into a physically readable reaction demonstrated by the host

beats.visual: Wide cream-paper illustration of a loose semicircle of three ordinary people, one mid-yawn and the other two beginning to mirror the gesture at slightly different stages, their bodies linked only by subtle curved graphite sightlines and repeated open-jaw shapes.
beats.purpose: show the recognizable phenomenon of one yawn being followed by others
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-person semicircle + staggered yawning stages + open neutral social space + curved sightline motifs + wide balanced composition
beats.continuity: expands from one host reaction to the broader social phenomenon involving several people

beats.narration_slice: It occurs in humans and some social animals.
beats.visual: Soft graphite storybook scene divided spatially without panels: a yawning human pair occupies the lower foreground while, farther up a grassy slope, two non-specific social mammals rest together with one opening its mouth in a yawn; muted moss and pale straw pencil tint unifies the scene.
beats.purpose: show that contagious-yawning-like behavior is observed in humans and some social animals
beats.visual_fingerprint: human pair foreground + social mammals on upper grassy slope + outdoor park setting + low-to-high vertical depth composition + dual-species action
beats.continuity: broadens the social group from humans alone to a species comparison in a new outdoor setting

beats.narration_slice: Social connection may influence who catches it.
beats.visual: Top-down graphite illustration of four people around a small café table: one yawns, a close companion beside them begins to yawn too, while two more distant acquaintances remain absorbed elsewhere; subtle proximity arcs and overlapping chair shadows suggest stronger connection without labels.
beats.purpose: show that social closeness may affect who responds to a yawn
beats.visual_fingerprint: bird's-eye café table + yawning adjacent pair + two disengaged companions + circular seating geometry + proximity suggested by overlapping shadows
beats.continuity: narrows the broad social observation into differences among individuals within one group

beats.narration_slice: But the exact mechanism remains unsettled.
beats.visual: The Red Horned Everyman stands beside a tabletop covered with loose pencil sketches of an eye, brain silhouette, jaw motion, and paired figures, studying several faint branching graphite paths that approach one another but never resolve into a single connection; his posture is calm and skeptical.
beats.purpose: show that multiple plausible explanations exist without one settled mechanism
beats.visual_fingerprint: Red Horned Everyman standing + scattered concept sketches on tabletop + branching unresolved graphite paths + high three-quarter camera angle + investigative composition
beats.continuity: pulls the earlier visual ideas together while deliberately leaving their relationship unresolved

beats.narration_slice: Evidence tying it directly to empathy is mixed.
beats.visual: Simple graphite balance-scale metaphor on warm cream paper: one pan holds two closely interacting human silhouettes and the other holds a yawning-face sketch, but the scale sits nearly level and visibly uncertain, surrounded by a few incomplete pencil marks rather than conclusions or labels.
beats.purpose: show that the proposed direct link between empathy and contagious yawning has mixed evidence
beats.visual_fingerprint: old-fashioned balance scale + paired social silhouettes on one pan + yawning-face sketch on other pan + sparse uncertain pencil marks + isolated centered composition
beats.continuity: moves from several unresolved mechanisms to one specifically uncertain proposed explanation

beats.narration_slice: So seeing a yawn can quietly set another in motion.
beats.visual: Side-on medium-wide view of two people on opposite benches at a quiet transit stop: the first is finishing a yawn while the second, after glancing over, is just beginning one; a delicate sequence of fading graphite jaw contours bridges the open space between them like a nearly invisible ripple.
beats.purpose: summarize the observable chain from seeing a yawn to beginning another
beats.visual_fingerprint: two opposite benches + first yawn ending and second beginning + transit-stop setting + fading jaw-contour ripple across negative space + side-profile composition
beats.continuity: returns from uncertainty to the simple observable effect the evidence does support

beats.narration_slice: One mouth opens, and another suddenly wants to.
beats.visual: Return to the opening workshop: the Red Horned Everyman sits beside the worn book and neatly sorted tools, caught in a small involuntary yawn while a second nearby person at the far edge of frame has just opened their mouth first; soft daylight and familiar cream-paper pencil texture close the visual loop.
beats.purpose: return to the opening situation and land the idea with one yawn immediately prompting another
beats.visual_fingerprint: opening workshop return + Red Horned Everyman seated beside worn book + nearby person already yawning + sorted tools as background accents + wide closing two-shot
beats.continuity: returns deliberately to the opening workshop for the final visual unit, completing the episode's closing mode
